$comment: ★★ A COMMON BESIDE MinGW's WEAK DEFINITION OF ITS NAME: THE COMMON STANDS (P69 send-back 5, review-xa4 MINOR 4; D-LK-COMMON-OUTRANKED-A-WEAK-DEFINITION-IN-EVERY-FORMAT) -- on the SAME format where cl's select-any replaces a common (`examples/c/common_beside_a_selectany_definition_pe`), because here the fact is the OBJECT's. The two objects named to the link are mingw-w64 gcc's builds of `int dss_tentative; int dss_read_tentative(void) { return dss_tentative; }` under `-fcommon` (a COMMON, with an `-aligncomm:` directive for it) and of `__attribute__((weak)) int dss_tentative = 5;`, which mingw-w64 gcc writes as a WEAK EXTERNAL over a body of its own (`.weak.dss_tentative.`): a name any other definition satisfies, a common included. ✔MEASURED 2026-10-08 (the same main.c built by mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0, GNU ld 2.42): in both object orders the common stands and the program reads 0, exit 37, as the common object alone does. The COFF reader states that on the definition it reads from a weak external's body (`ModuleSymbol::yieldsToACommon`), and the link's one answer (`linker::commonYieldsToDefinition`) lets the common outrank it whatever the format document says of other definitions. main.c is DSS's; the 37 it adds keeps either answer apart from the exit code of a program that did nothing -- a link that let the 5 through would exit 42. The `release` arm pins that optimizing the DSS half changes nothing about which of the two the program reads.

prebuiltLibraries.$comment: The COMMON, and the function that reads it. Source and rebuild command: `tests/link/data/tentative_common.source.c` (mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 `-O2 -fcommon -c`; md5 119be2569ac83657b3c21e358b69f3d3). A relocatable object named to the link is an OBJECT INPUT, linked eagerly. The witness is the reader's name.

The WEAK definition. Source and rebuild command: `tests/link/data/tentative_weak.source.c` (mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 `-O2 -c`; md5 4d2a95faa99961f854de10103995c462). The witness is the name of the body the weak external stands over: an object that defines `dss_tentative` any other way cannot pass.
